c: Coordinates instruction execution and the CPU's internal operations.

m.title: CPU Architecture and the Fetch-Execute Cycle
m.q: Trace how the PC, MAR and MDR participate in fetching an instruction.
st: PC holds the address of the next instruction.
The address is copied to MAR.
The instruction at that address is transferred to MDR.
The instruction is decoded/executed, and PC is updated as appropriate.

k.q: Predict the value held in acc.
p: Explain your predicted result using the first assignment or test.
Explain that the variable acc models a running result; state what the CPU's ACC register actually stores.
k.a: The output is 10; changing +6 to +8 gives 12. The variable acc is not a physical CPU register. The accumulator (ACC) is a CPU register that can hold results of arithmetic or logical calculations.

e: State the purpose of MAR and MDR. [4 marks]
MAR: address of memory location accessed; MDR: data/instruction being transferred.
What does the Program Counter hold? [1 mark]
Address of the next instruction to fetch.
Explain the role of the Control Unit. [2 marks]
Coordinates CPU operations and controls execution of instructions.
v: Coordinates instruction execution and the CPU's internal operations.
PC stores next instruction address, MAR stores address accessed, MDR holds transferred data/instruction and ACC holds calculation results.
Instruction fetches from memory, decodes, executes and the cycle repeats.
x: The MDR stores the address of the next instruction.
r: Differentiate a syntax error from a logic error.
Syntax violates language rules; logic produces incorrect behaviour even if program runs.
A student's trace omits the final loop iteration. Explain the impact.
The last update is missed, so the final recorded state and possibly output are incorrect.
State the difference between concatenation and arithmetic addition.
Concatenation joins string content; arithmetic addition calculates a numerical sum.
State why expected outcomes belong in a test plan.
They allow actual results to be compared with requirements and faults detected.

mastery.task: Given PC=42 and an instruction stored at address 42, create a simple fetch-stage register trace identifying when MAR and MDR change. Explain why ACC need not change during fetch.
mastery.hint: PC supplies next address; MAR stores address; MDR receives fetched instruction.
mastery.answer: PC initially42; MAR←42; MDR←memory[42]; PC updated according to instruction length/sequencing; no arithmetic result needed, so ACC need not change. Correct answers distinguish address from data.
